Pinterest Setup, Pins and Strategy

Pinterest Strategy for Bloggers

By Marie Glow StudioPublished August 3, 2026Updated September 26, 2026

A blog post you wrote eight months ago can still be your best-performing Pinterest destination, if you link to it the right way. A Pinterest strategy for bloggers uses Pinterest as an evergreen discovery channel: match each article to a real search, then create several distinct pins that lead into it.

How should bloggers group posts for Pinterest?

Group your posts into keyword clusters, where each cluster covers one topic a reader might search for. A cluster gives you a natural board, a set of related pins and posts that can point to each other. Scattered posts on unrelated topics are harder to organize and harder for Pinterest to understand.

Which articles make the best pin destinations?

Articles that answer a complete question make the best destinations, because the visitor gets what the pin promised. Lead with the posts that are genuinely helpful and let the thinner ones wait. A pin that opens on a useful, finished answer gives a reader a reason to stay and to click further. Point each pin at the specific post rather than at the front page of your blog or your homepage, so the reader lands on the answer without having to search for it.

How many pins can one blog post support?

A strong article can support several pins, as long as each pin has its own concept. One might pose the question, another might list the steps, another might promise the finished result. Treat each as a separate entry point to the same post. Designing pins that get clicks covers what makes an individual pin work.

How do related posts and email keep readers going?

Link related posts to each other so a visitor who finishes one article has an obvious next read. Add evergreen boards that hold your ongoing topics, and give the reader a path to your email list or an offer when it fits. Pinterest and email marketing working together shows how discovery turns into a subscriber.

What should a Pinterest strategy for bloggers start with?

Start with one cluster rather than the whole archive. Pick a topic such as Pinterest SEO for handmade product businesses, choose the most helpful post in it, and make two or three different pins that point to that post. Then link the cluster's other posts to each other and check the numbers before adding a second cluster.

When should you refresh an older post?

Refresh the posts that already bring search and click activity, since those have proven interest. Check which articles earn saves and outbound clicks, update anything that is dated, and give the best performers new pin concepts. Because a pin can stay searchable long after it goes up, an updated post can keep earning attention for a good while.

How do you measure what Pinterest does for a blog?

Track saves and outbound clicks for each pin, then use your blog analytics to see whether visitors from Pinterest read further, follow a related link or join your list. Compare pins that point to the same post to learn which concept draws more interest. Judge them across enough time to see a pattern, since a single week can mislead.

Can you hand this work off?

Yes. Monthly Pinterest Management from Marie Glow Studio is a done-for-you service for people with blog posts, courses or products worth promoting who lack the time to run Pinterest. It includes keyword research, content planning, custom branded pins and scheduling. If your posts sell a digital offer, Pinterest marketing for digital products is the natural companion read.

Results vary with your niche, competition, seasonality and how consistently you publish, and none of it can be guaranteed. What you can control is giving every strong post more than one way in.

Frequently asked questions

Can old blog posts still work on Pinterest?

Yes. Older pins can keep surfacing in search and sometimes gain visibility later, although every pin's lifespan varies. Refresh the posts that already earn saves and clicks first.

How many pins should one blog post have?

Several, as long as each pin has a distinct concept. A strong article can be reached from more than one angle, such as a question, a list of steps or a finished result.
